newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil steady on quiet Euro vegetable oil market.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil steady on quiet Euro vegetable oil market.

text.p: Palm oil prices were mostly steady at midday on Friday on the European vegetable oil market supported by the higher close in the Far East.
After a choppy session the Malaysian market finished mostly higher despite a lack of any fresh news.
Most crop reports which were due for release in the next few days have been delayed by the Chinese New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr holidays.

Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) stock, output and export data for January scheduled for release on February 15 has been put back until February 22 while private forecaster Ivan Wong will now release his report next week instead of this morning.
Traders said the delay to these reports and the U.S. holiday on Monday will lead to a slow start to business next week.
"It could be the middle of next week before things get going again, but even than you will find people who want to see the PORLA data before making fresh commitments," said a trader.
Crude palm oil cif Europe was offered $5 up to unchanged at midday after Mar traded at $585 and $587.50, Apr/Jun at $575 and Oct/Dec at $560 a tonne cif in early business.
Among products RBD oil was $2.50 up to $2.50 down after Mar traded at $567.50 while olein was unchanged to $2.50 higher and tradeless.
Coconut oil and palmkernel oil sellers were $2.50 higher with no business reported so far.
Soft oils were also quiet with soy oil sellers 0.25 to one guilder up and rape oil unchanged to 0.50 guilders higher.
EU sunfloweroil was around $5 up at midday with no follow-through business seen from Thursday.
